# serial_cmd.sh -- send commands to the board and capture the reply.
#
# Why a helper: every debug round needs "reset, get into the AP shell, run a
# command, read the output".  Doing that by hand through screen is not
# scriptable and loses the log; doing it ad hoc with cat/printf gets the
# ordering subtly wrong (the reader has to be running *before* the write, or
# the first output is lost).
#
# The console is at 115200 -- fixed by the CP build
# (bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config:
# CONFIG_UART_PRINT_BAUD_RATE=115200).  Do not confuse it with autoflash.sh's
# -b, which is only the bootrom download rate.
#
# Usage:
#   serial_cmd.sh [-r] [-w SECONDS] [-e PATTERN] [-o LOGFILE] 'cmd1' 'cmd2' ...
#
#   -r            reboot first, and enter the AP console before the commands
#   -w SECONDS    how long to keep reading after the last command (default 6)
#   -e PATTERN    stop reading as soon as PATTERN (grep -E) shows up in the
#                 log, instead of always waiting the full -w.  -w stays the
#                 upper bound.  Use the command's own last line, e.g.
#                 -e 'agent_camera: OK'.  Without this, a run that needs a
#                 large -w to be safe always pays that -w even when the board
#                 finished in a second.
#   -o LOGFILE    where to save the transcript (default /tmp/serial_cmd.log)
#
# Commands are sent one per line with a short gap, so the shell has time to
# echo its prompt between them.

set -u

PORT=/dev/ttyUSB0
# 2026-08-13: upstream moved the CP console from 921600 to 115200 (see
# external/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config and upstream's
# own autoflash.sh, which also uses CONSOLE_BAUD=115200).  Reading at the old
# rate returns 0x80/0x00 garbage, which looks exactly like a dead board.
BAUD=115200
WAIT=6
LOG=/tmp/serial_cmd.log
DO_RESET=0
STOP_RE=

while getopts "rw:o:p:e:" opt; do
  case "$opt" in
    r) DO_RESET=1 ;;
